# Lab 22.1: Create a BI Engine Reservation

## What We Are Going to Do
Reserve BI Engine memory, set a preferred table, and compare query speed with and without acceleration. BI Engine memory is billed per GiB-hour, so delete it at the end of Lab 22.3.

## Steps

1. **[SQL] Create a dashboard-sized table.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS lab22 OPTIONS (location = 'US');

CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE lab22.sales AS
SELECT DATE(i.created_at) AS day, p.category, p.brand, u.country, i.sale_price, i.status
FROM `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.order_items` i
JOIN `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.products` p ON p.id = i.product_id
JOIN `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.users` u ON u.id = i.user_id;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


2. **[SQL] Run a dashboard query before BI Engine.** Turn off the cache in Query settings.


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">SELECT country, category, ROUND(SUM(sale_price), 2) AS revenue
FROM lab22.sales WHERE status = 'Complete'
GROUP BY country, category ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 20;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   Note the elapsed time.

3. **[SQL] Create the BI Engine reservation with a preferred table.** Replace `YOUR_PROJECT`.


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">ALTER BI_CAPACITY `YOUR_PROJECT.region-us.default`
SET OPTIONS (
  size_gb = 1,
  preferred_tables = ['YOUR_PROJECT.lab22.sales']
);</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   With preferred tables set, only those tables use the reserved memory.

4. **[Console] See it in the UI.** **Administration → BI Engine**. The reservation shows 1 GiB in `US` and the preferred table.

5. **[SQL] Run the query from step 2 again.** It is faster, and the job details show BI Engine was used.

6. **[CLI] Check the BI Engine capacity from bq.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">bq query --use_legacy_sql=false 'SELECT * FROM `region-us`.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.BI_CAPACITIES'</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Reservation | 1 GiB in `US` |
| Preferred table | `lab22.sales` |
| Speed | Lower elapsed time |
| Cost | Memory billed per GiB-hour |
